subject: Information Theory
title: How Your Ears Work
description: A short lesson to help you apply How Your Ears Work.

hook.text: Your inner ear contains 3,500 hair cells arranged by frequency—a biological Fourier transform running constantly.

buildup.text: Sound enters the cochlea. High frequencies vibrate near the base, low frequencies near the tip.

discovery.text: Each hair cell responds to a narrow frequency band. Together, they decompose sound into its frequency components.

twist.text: Your brain reassembles these frequencies into voices, music, and warnings—all in milliseconds, using neural processing.

climax.text: Cochlear implants replicate this: they stimulate hair cells electrically, restoring hearing through signal processing.

punchline.text: Your ear is a spectrum analyzer. Evolution built it first.

quiz.question: How does the cochlea process sound?
options: Different positions respond to different frequencies
